title: The Missing Diplomat: From Stormwind to Alcaz
summary: A quiet inquiry reveals Stormwind’s missing king. A later search among a wreck and Alcaz’s marshes deepens the mystery without naming the powerful patron behind it.
opening: A sealed letter leaves Stormwind Keep and passes through trusted hands. From Duskwood’s farms to the Wetlands harbor and Theramore, the search finds a suspect while the king remains absent. Another inquiry opens among wreckage and the rune-marked pools of Alcaz.

chapters.title: A quiet commission
chapters.body:
At the Cathedral of Light, Thomas asked for an adventurer who could keep a matter private. Bishop DeLavey waited within Stormwind Keep. The request sounded small, yet carried a greater burden: someone within the kingdom had chosen discretion before disclosure. Among the city’s familiar streets, a quiet inquiry began without the public alarm its hidden purpose might have raised.

A diplomat sent to Theramore had never reached Lady Jaina Proudmoore. Bishop DeLavey spoke of an absence not yet commonly known. The king’s agents were searching, but the bishop set his own contacts in motion. A sealed letter went first to Jorgen, a fisherman in the Valley of Heroes. The search had a destination, though no culprit.

Jorgen recognized the bishop’s seal and reluctantly accepted the duty. He wrote to Elling Trias, asking that the confidence placed in him remain intact. From a church office through a fisherman, trust carried the inquiry toward a man who traded in information. No weapon had been drawn. The search advanced through people who knew how to keep a name quiet.

Elling Trias sent the search toward Watcher Backus in Duskwood. Unusual Defias activity offered a lead without yet explaining the Brotherhood’s part in the disappearance. Stormwind’s pale walls gave way to wooded country, where old farms stood beneath fog. Each handoff narrowed the inquiry while leaving its purpose uncertain, carrying the bishop’s confidence into another keeper’s hands.

Backus remembered unusual Defias activity around Addle’s Stead. A search among the dark fields yielded a docket from a chest. He recognized the papers as authentic, but the matter had passed beyond local watchwork. The evidence returned to Elling. Among Duskwood’s secluded farms, the search had recovered writing whose wider meaning waited upon someone who knew the names it carried.

Elling found Dashel Stonefist’s name in the docket. A resident of Stormwind’s Old Town had become the next lead. From papers hidden beneath Duskwood’s canopy, the inquiry returned to familiar streets and guarded reputations. The danger had not passed. Its next door lay within the city, where Elling’s knowledge could turn a written trace into someone who might answer.

chapters.title: A docket in Duskwood
chapters.body:
Dashel admitted that an earlier plan had failed and named Tapoke “Slim” Jahn in another. The search turned north toward Menethil Harbor. From the woods, the trail reached the Wetlands’ cold coast and an inn where Slim might remain unnoticed. A failed operation had left a loose end, carrying the inquiry toward a man who knew more of the vanished voyage.

At the Menethil inn, Slim learned that Elling’s inquiry had reached him. He tried to escape, and a brief struggle ended with his capture. Amid the damp harbor’s crowded rooms and docks, a quiet search had met a suspect who could no longer keep his distance. The questions that had passed through sealed letters could now be put to the man himself.

chapters.title: The missing king
chapters.body:
Slim gave up the name at the center of the search. The missing diplomat was Varian Wrynn, Stormwind’s king. Hendel, he said, had been meant to board the royal ship. The trail now bore the weight of a kingdom’s absence. Yet naming the king and an intended accomplice had not brought Varian home, or revealed what had become of his voyage.

The harbor inquiry pointed toward Commander Samaul in Theramore. Kul Tiras marines travelled from there to Menethil on leave, and Elling’s name could earn the commander’s confidence. From the damp northern docks, the search crossed the sea toward Dustwallow’s fortified port. A military posting offered the next lead, while the vanished king’s own passage remained unknown.

Commander Samaul hesitated before trusting a stranger. Then he named Hendel’s last post: Sentry Point, the first tower beyond Theramore. The outpost watched marsh and shore between the city and the uncertain coast. One soldier now stood at the center of the inquiry, though the commander could not settle what he knew of the plan Slim had described.

At Sentry Point, Archmage Tervosh said Jaina knew of the inquiry and had directed him to help. Hendel was west of the tower, watching Theramore’s scouts return from their search for Brackenwall. The marsh had yielded the soldier’s position. Beyond the watchtower, the investigator approached a man already named in the plan surrounding Varian’s ship.

Hendel resisted, and nearby guards joined the struggle. The adventurer subdued him; Tervosh and Jaina arrived to take him into custody. The search had found a participant whose name was tied to Varian’s ship. It had not found the king. Across the marsh coast, the central disappearance remained unresolved, and the captive still held questions the investigation could not yet answer.

Jaina gave the adventurer her signet ring in thanks. Hendel was held for questioning, but Varian remained absent. The search had passed through Stormwind, Duskwood, the Wetlands and the marsh coast, carrying a quiet appeal into a royal mystery. Its discoveries had reached Theramore without recovering the missing king, and the full purpose behind his disappearance remained beyond their knowledge.

chapters.title: Cargo beneath the marsh
chapters.body:
Another report brought the Defias into view along the Dreadmurk Shore. Lieutenant Aden spoke of survivors near a shipwreck and sent the investigator to Captain Wymor at Sentry Point. A new inquiry began among scattered timbers and coastal waters. If the wreck belonged to the Brotherhood, its cargo might explain what had drawn them so far from their usual ground.

Wymor’s scouts had seen red-bandana Defias near the wreck, far from their Stormwind dealings. On a nearby island, Garn Mathers held an order to protect the cargo at any cost, with payment promised for success and silence. The patron remained unnamed. Wymor sent the writing to Renn McGill, a salvage diver already searching the shore.

Renn confirmed that Defias divers worked among the wreckage. The orders gave him reason to search before they could recover its hidden burden. Broken timbers stretched toward Alcaz through dangerous naga-held waters. Diving gear and tools had to be recovered and repaired. Beneath the waterline, the lost cargo became a trail the investigator could physically follow.

From the broken ship, salvaged strongboxes brought coins, jewelry and letters to the surface. Among the remnants, Renn found enchanted iron manacles. The cargo had included more than valuables: someone had been bound aboard. The cold restraints changed the search, drawing the wreck’s hidden burden nearer the old question of Varian’s disappearance without yet revealing whom they had held.

Renn urged that the manacles be brought to Jaina at once. They showed that a prisoner had been restrained, but could not name that person or reveal their fate. Above the marsh and sea, Theramore’s pale walls sheltered the weighing of another clue. The vanished voyage now stood beside evidence drawn from the wreck, while the greater design remained hidden.

chapters.title: The island and the patron
chapters.body:
Jaina judged Renn’s suspicion about Alcaz worth examining. A large force would overstrain Theramore’s defenses, so she arranged a flight with Cassa Crimsonwing, an apprentice gryphon handler. Knowledge had to come before another commitment of troops. From above the marsh, the island could be observed while its defenders and their purposes remained unknown.

The gryphon passed above Alcaz’s wet, broken ground. Below lay a rune circle, black dragons, naga, hydras and human figures among the marsh pools. The island was crowded with danger. From above, the observer could see their presence without knowing what ties bound them, or what purpose had gathered them upon that uncertain shore.

Jaina believed Defias hedge magic could not explain Alcaz’s rune circle. The island’s inhabitants raised questions she could not settle. Yet she suspected a powerful ally high within the Alliance and tied the plan to Varian’s disappearance. The inquiry had reached beyond the Brotherhood’s own means, leaving a greater patron unnamed behind the missing king’s fate.

Jaina’s findings reached Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. He took the report seriously and planned renewed action against the Defias until the king returned. Lady Katrana Prestor urged him elsewhere, dismissing the charge as speculation. Within Stormwind Keep, the island’s unanswered questions met a divided response. Bolvar asked that Jaina receive his thanks, while the patron she suspected remained unnamed.

The messenger returned to Jaina with Bolvar’s answer. The manacles had revealed a prisoner’s passage; Alcaz had yielded a rune circle and a troubling gathering. Jaina believed a powerful Alliance patron stood behind the Defias. Yet the patron remained unnamed and Varian remained missing. The search ended with thanks and suspicion, carrying its unanswered royal absence back to Theramore.

reviewNote: Complete 24-scene illustrated research story with source-linked event, claim and citation records; separate Classic and patch 2.3 boundaries; original interpretive character and location art; Stormwind, Duskwood, Wetlands, Theramore, Dreadmurk and Alcaz scenes; and transcript-matched voice-over. StoryTour placement after the Outland Cipher is editorial because this story’s final playable segment was added in patch 2.3; the original Classic chain remains an earlier subperiod. At the story boundary Varian remains missing and the patron is unnamed. Do not conflate either chain with The Great Masquerade, the later Proof of Treachery, comics, Varian’s rescue, or an Onyxia plot. Human source review, original-client comparison, game-area resemblance review and audio audition remain open. Content remains research and never implies exact dates, routes, or co-presence.
